comment_body: Using a controllable promise pattern for async tests is a great approach. It allows for precise control over when the promise resolves, making tests more deterministic and easier to debug.
Good test coverage for basic arithmetic operations. Consider adding edge cases like very large numbers or floating point precision tests.
The division by zero test is important. Make sure the error message is user-friendly and consider logging the error for debugging purposes.
This async test pattern using controllable promises is excellent for testing race conditions and timeout scenarios. Well implemented!
Good test for the reset functionality. This ensures the calculator state is properly cleaned up between operations.

## Overall Assessment

This PR adds comprehensive unit tests for the Calculator utility class. The test coverage is good, with tests for basic operations, error handling, and async functionality.

### Strengths
- Clean test structure using describe/test blocks
- Good use of beforeEach/afterEach for setup and teardown
- Controllable promise pattern for async testing

### Areas for Improvement
- Consider adding boundary value tests
- Add tests for concurrent operations
- Consider memory management for history feature
